title: Lacson flags P241B in 'fragmented ayuda' in 2027 budget
summary: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Sunday criticized P241 billion worth of fragmented assistance programs in the Senate version of the proposed 2027 national budget, saying these would not generate the…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Sunday criticized P241 billion worth of fragmented assistance programs in the Senate version of the proposed 2027 national budget, saying these would not generate the productive investments needed to revive the economy.
In a social media post, Lacson said the amount was already lower than the P263 billion allocated for similar items in the House version of the General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

"True. Government construction plunged by -29% as shown by the January-September 2026 national accounts. Agriculture, forestry and fishing: -4.8%; industry: flat; investment: public construction down 15.1% as you mentioned," the senator said.

Lacson said the Senate should reconsider the allocations, arguing that the P241 billion in "fragmented" aid programs and funding for thousands of multipurpose buildings would not address the country's economic concerns.

"In relation to the 2027 budget measure which the Senate will tackle next week, I will insist that these concerns cannot be addressed by the P241B in fragmented ‘ayudas’ in the Senate version - already reduced from the House GAB’s P263B; and 3,950 multi-purpose buildings, on top of another 1,584 MPB’s under the LGSF-Financial Assistance to LGU sub program," he said.
These are not expenditure investments, but patronage aka ‘papogi’ spending," Lacson added.
He also questioned funding for 3,950 multipurpose buildings (MPBs), on top of 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) from 2022 to 2026.
Lacson said these allocations were examples of patronage-driven spending rather than productive investments, which the government should prioritize amid slowing economic growth and rising inflation.
He cited the 2.1% gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the third quarter of 2026, down from 2.4% in the second quarter, as well as inflation rising to 7.8% in October from 7.2% in September.

The senator also questioned allocations for the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP), Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) and Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS).
He said funding for MAIFIP should instead be coursed through the Universal Health Care program, which is already mandated by law.
Lacson argued that these assistance programs were not needs-based, claiming that beneficiaries were often determined by their connections to political sponsors rather than their eligibility.

“Again, this is patronage-driven. Those who benefit are the ones with connections. It is not needs-based. It is like having a sponsor or a political backer who gets you assistance, even if you are not qualified or deserving,” he said.

Initial findings on the proposed 2027 budget also showed that several multipurpose buildings had received appropriations in 2024, 2025 and 2026, but no structures had been built at their designated sites as of 2026.
Lacson said the Senate should prioritize spending that would stimulate economic activity when it takes up the 2027 budget measure next week.— MCG, GMA News
